When no nav tool is latched, the PR's ball-press guard (`move_drag::press`) runs as before, so a press on a ball does not pick or orbit. The Escape cancel, the release routing, the motion routing and the handle draw call merged with no conflict.

Result: the move stays one `MoveModelBy` command with one undo step. If a nav tool is latched, a left press goes to that tool and not to a move ball.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 553f6c2e631d638f344c93458e43e3d71f33e464 -->
**Verdict: blockers**

Full review of head `553f6c2e6` against `AGENTS.md` and `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`. Read from the diff. Not built.

## Blockers

1. **Derived data is computed again in each frame, three times.** `crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs:88` (`shown_center`) transforms every facet of the part to get its bounding-box centre. `handles()` (`move_drag.rs:124`) calls it, and `arms_px()` (`move_drag.rs:143`) calls `handles()`. While Move mode is on and a part is selected, the paint code calls `arms_px` one time and `ball_at` two times in each frame (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs:14`, `:21`, `:38`). Each `ball_at` call runs `arms_px` again. Thus each frame transforms all the facets three times, also when the pointer does not move. On a large imported part this can use the full frame budget (frame target under 10 ms, #2238). Derived data must be calculated one time and kept.
   - Fix: keep the centre in a small cache that is keyed on the part entity, `doc_version` and the active setup. Or calculate `arms_px` one time for each frame and give the result to `ball_at` and to the cursor check.

## Non-blocking findings

1. **Focus loss does not cancel a drag.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs:529` and `:559` act on `body_drag` without a check of the pane or of the window focus. If the window loses focus while the button is down (Alt+Tab), the release can go to a different window. Then the preview follows the pointer, and the next primary release anywhere sends `MoveModelBy`. The result is visible and it is one undo step, so it is not unsafe. Recommended: cancel the drag on `!i.focused` or on `PointerGone`, and add a test. I did not examine if egui itself releases the button on focus loss.
2. **A near edge-on axis can give a very large jump.** `move_drag.rs:182` refuses a ray only when `sin^2` of the angle between the ray and the axis is less than about `1e-9`. Just above that limit, `t` can be very large (metres or more) for a small pointer motion. The value is finite, so `document_target` accepts it. Recommended: clamp `delta` for each frame (for example to a multiple of the part size or of the view size), or hold the last value when the angle is less than a few degrees.
3. **File size.** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar.rs` grows from 433 to 461 lines, and `shell.rs` from 1055 to 1070. Both were more than 400 lines on `main`. Recommended: a `P7` follow-up to split the bar glyph painter out of `viewport_bar.rs`.
4. **Glyph.** The PR body says that the Move glyph and the Pan glyph look almost the same. I agree. A different glyph for Move (for example arms with balls on three axes) is better. This is not a blocker.
5. **Label state.** The PR has the `conflicts` label, but a trial merge (`git merge-tree`) of this head with the current `origin/main` is clean.

## Checks that pass

- **Everything Is a Command.** A press on a ball writes only `State::body_drag` (view state). The preview offsets only the drawn vertices (`world.rs` `world_verts_by`) and writes no document field. The release (`move_drag.rs:210`) queues exactly one `CommandKind::MoveModelBy`. `state_move_by.rs` turns it into one `MoveModel::new` plus one `history.execute`, the same as the Model page arm. Escape, Move off, and a release with `|delta| <= 1e-6` queue nothing. Tests: `a_ball_drag_is_one_undoable_move_by_the_dragged_distance`, `escape_mid_drag_cancels_with_no_history_step`, `a_drag_that_ends_where_it_began_adds_nothing`.
- **Staleness.** The drag uses the same `MoveModel` command and the same `doc_version += 1` as the existing `MoveModel` arm. Operations read the changed placement and become stale (`crates/app/src/commands/move_model.rs:22`). The drag makes no second placement path. The rotation is copied bit for bit (`the_rotation_is_kept_bit_for_bit`), so no stock re-fit from an Euler round trip.
- **Numeric safety.** A non-finite delta, an unknown part and a non-finite target are refused with a status message (`a_non_finite_distance_is_refused_by_name`). `px_per_mm` and `aspect` refuse a zero size. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests.
- **Layers.** The UI code uses `camcraft_app::model` and `setup_align` read helpers and the command history. No `sys_*` call.
- **Strings.** "Move: drag a ball on the selected part", "Move: off" and "moved Block by X +12.500 mm" are plain English. The glyph is painted, no new icon asset.
- **Tests.** Ten new tests (5 kittest, 5 headless). No test removed. No new page or window, so no new layout test is necessary; `bar_fits_its_buttons` covers the wider bar. No snapshot PNG changed.
- **Merge resolution.** `git show --remerge-diff` shows two hand edits. `state.rs` keeps the two module lines. `shell.rs` keeps the `frame_cost::time` wrapper of `main` and adds `|| state.body_drag.is_some()`. Both are correct.
- **PR body.** Screenshots, `Changelog:` line, `Refs #1198`, and an MCP statement are present. The MCP statement is correct: `move_model` in `crates/app/src/mcp/model_tools.rs:29` places a part through `MoveModel`, and `MoveModelBy` is only a UI queue verb.

Review fix for comment 6976973927. New head: `3d394d6f474ca087706886dd00c4469d212248b1` (one commit on `553f6c2e6`).

**Blocker: `shown_center` walked every facet, three times each frame.**
- `crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs` 87-141: a new `CenterCache` keeps the centre. The field is `State::move_center` (a `Mutex`, because the handles read `&State`).
- The key is the input itself: the entity, the facet `Arc` and the shown pose, bit for bit. A move, an undo, a setup switch or a geometry change gives a new key. The key does not use `doc_version` alone, because the frame-cost law (#2238, `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`) forbids that key.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`: the paint code computes the arms one time each frame. The new `move_drag::ball_in` (`move_drag.rs` 205-216) finds the hot ball and the cursor from those arms.
- Test: `move_drag_tests::a_still_frame_walks_no_facets_and_a_move_walks_them_again`. Ten calls on an unchanged document do not walk the facets again. A `MoveModelBy` walks them one time, and the centre is the new one.

**Small fix: a drag is cancelled on focus loss.**
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` 526-535: `Event::WindowFocused(false)`, `Event::PointerGone` or `!focused` drops the drag. A later release sends no move.
- Test: `egui_app::tests::body_drag::focus_loss_mid_drag_cancels_and_a_later_release_sends_no_move`.

**Small fix: an axis seen almost end-on.**
- `move_drag.rs` 218-260: the new pure function `ray_axis_t` refuses a cursor ray within 3 degrees of the axis. The drag then holds its last value.
- `clamp_step` limits one motion step to one view width in mm.
- Tests: `move_drag_tests::an_axis_seen_almost_end_on_holds_the_drag` (0, 1 and 2.9 degrees are held; 10 and 90 degrees give the exact value; NaN is refused) and `move_drag_tests::one_motion_step_drags_at_most_one_view_width` (the pure clamp and the live `motion` path).

**Not in this change:** the file splits and the icon. The follow-up issue holds them.

**Gate** on `3d394d6f4` (debug, `-j 6`):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 17 steps, 0 failed, 4.6 min. This includes the camcraft-ui lib step.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings`: clean.

The PR body test list now names the 4 new tests.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 3d394d6f474ca087706886dd00c4469d212248b1 -->
**Verdict: blockers**

Re-review of the one review-fix commit `3d394d6f4` on `553f6c2e6` (earlier review: comment 6976973927). The range holds only this commit. `git merge-tree` of this head with the current `origin/main` is clean. Read from the diff. Not built.

## Blocker

1. **The commit changes the line ends of four files from LF to CRLF.** Each line of these files is in the diff:
   - `crates/ui/src/state.rs`: 4798 lines (the logical change is 5 lines).
   - `crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`: 343 lines.
   - `crates/ui/src/move_drag_tests.rs`: 178 lines.
   - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`: 44 lines.

   On `origin/main` and on `553f6c2e6` these files have LF line ends (0 CR bytes). The trial-merge tree keeps the CRLF line ends. `git diff --stat` shows 9591 changed lines in `state.rs`. Eight other open PRs change `state.rs` (#2488, #2484, #2448, #2256, #2253, #2185, #2149, #1798). After this PR merges, each of them conflicts on the full file. The change also removes the `git blame` history of `state.rs`.
   - Fix: write the four files again with LF line ends (for example `git add --renormalize` with `core.autocrlf=input`, or `dos2unix` on the four files), commit, and push. Then `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol` and `git diff` must give the same `--stat` (199 lines changed). No logic change is necessary.

## The delta (logic): correct

1. **Centre cache** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs` 90-129, `State::move_center`).
   - The key is the entity, the facet `Arc` (held, compared with `Arc::ptr_eq`) and the 7 pose words bit for bit. This obeys `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` "Frame cost": the key is the input, never `doc_version` alone. The worker's reason is correct.
   - A move, an undo, a redo and a setup switch change the shown pose (`setup_align::view_pose`), thus the key. A geometry change or a model reload gives a new `Arc`. Because the cache holds the old `Arc`, its address cannot be used again, and an in-place `Arc::make_mut` must clone. A part delete removes the part from `draggable`, so no handles show for it. I found no path to a stale centre.
   - The cache has one entry. The lock uses `unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)`; no `unwrap` or `expect`. The lock is held only for the compare and the facet walk, with no callback inside.
   - A counter test and a changed-input test are present (`a_still_frame_walks_no_facets_and_a_move_walks_them_again`). If the cache is bypassed, `computes` increases on each call and the test fails.
2. **One walk per frame.** `move_handles::draw` calls `arms_px` one time and `ball_in` uses that result for the hot ball and for the cursor. The other callers (`press`, `motion` in `shell.rs` 507 and 571) run on an input event only, and they read the cache. No other per-frame facet walk remains on this path. `draggable` reads the entity list each frame; that is not a facet walk.
3. **End-on hold and step clamp** (`move_drag.rs` 218-260, 273-283).
   - `ray_axis_t` refuses a ray within 3 degrees of the axis. A NaN or a zero direction fails `c > 1e-24 && denom >= END_ON_SIN2 * c`, and the result must be finite.
   - `clamp_step` holds the last value for a non-finite or non-positive limit. `motion` writes only a finite value.
   - The release is unchanged: one `MoveModelBy` for `|delta| > MIN_MOVE_MM`, else nothing. Thus one undo step.
4. **Focus loss** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` 526-535). `!focused`, `WindowFocused(false)` or `PointerGone` cancels the drag before the release arm. A later release finds no drag and queues nothing. The test `focus_loss_mid_drag_cancels_and_a_later_release_sends_no_move` checks the history and the part position.
5. **Tests.** Four new tests, each meaningful. No test is deleted or ignored. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Earlier findings (comment 6976973927)

| Finding | State |
|---|---|
| Blocker: `shown_center` walked every facet three times each frame | closed |
| Focus loss does not cancel a drag | closed |
| Near end-on axis gives a very large jump | closed |
| File size: `viewport_bar.rs` 461 lines, `shell.rs` now 1080 lines | open-non-blocking (follow-up issue, by decision) |
| The Move glyph looks almost the same as the Pan glyph | open-non-blocking (follow-up issue, by decision) |
| `conflicts` label on a head that merges cleanly | open-non-blocking (label state; maintainer) |

## New non-blocking finding

- The cache keeps the facet `Arc` of the last part that showed handles until a different key replaces it. When that part is deleted, or when Move mode goes off, the mesh stays in memory (one entry, so it is bounded). Recommended for the follow-up issue: clear `move_center` when `handles` finds no draggable part.

File lengths at this head: `move_drag.rs` 343, `move_drag_tests.rs` 178, `move_handles.rs` 44, `body_drag.rs` 179 lines.
